newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danisco sees sugar output slightly up.
newsitem.headline: Danisco sees sugar output slightly up.

text.p: Danish packaging, foods, drinks and sugar group Danisco A/S said on Wednesday that it expected its total sugar production for 1996 to be around one million tonnes, up slightly on its EU quota and 1995.
Danisco, Europe's fourth biggest sugar producer, with factories in Denmark, Sweden and Germany, attributed its forecast in part to the relatively higher sugar content in this harvest's beet.
Danisco's European Union sugar quota was set at a total 921,000 tonnes for this year, against 1995's output in all three countries of around a total 922,000 tonnes.

It said its Danisco Sugar unit in Denmark expected production fairly solidly in excess of the EU quota of 425,000 tonnes, with Danisco AB in Sweden also seen exceeding its individual EU quota of 370,000 tonnes and German Danisco Sugar GmbH producing more than its 126,000 EU quota.

Danisco's total sugar production turnover for 1996/97's first six months was put at 3.097 billion crowns, against the same 1995/96 period'd 3.058 billion crowns, with operating profit at 446 million crowns against 441 million crowns a year ago, it said.
The sugar production data appeared in a statement accompanying Danisco's group interim 1996/97 result.
Last September, Danisco forecast that its overall sugar production in the three countries in which it operates, would be the same or slightly higher than in 1995.
